items.stem: A team is choosing what to build next. Which approach is most aligned with value-driven delivery?

options.text: Build the easiest items first regardless of value
options.rationale: Ease is not the primary ordering criterion.

options.text: Order the backlog so the highest-value, highest-risk items come first
options.rationale: Correct: value-driven delivery front-loads value and risk reduction.

options.text: Build every requested feature before release
options.rationale: That delays value and contradicts incremental delivery.

options.text: Let the newest request always take priority

items.explanation: Correct: value-driven delivery front-loads value and risk reduction.

items.stem: What is the main purpose of a retrospective?

options.text: To inspect the team's process and agree improvements
options.rationale: Correct: retrospectives drive continuous improvement of the process.

options.text: To demo the product to stakeholders
options.rationale: That is a review, not a retrospective.

options.text: To finalise the fixed project plan

items.explanation: Correct: retrospectives drive continuous improvement of the process.

items.stem: Select TWO practices that support adaptive planning.

options.text: Re-planning each iteration based on observed velocity
options.rationale: Correct: using actual velocity to re-plan is adaptive planning.

options.text: Locking the scope at project start
Progressive elaboration of requirements over time
options.rationale: Correct: elaborating detail just in time is adaptive.

options.text: Refusing to change the release plan

options.rationale: Estimates are revised as information improves.
